title: What is a sanctuary city?
content:
I wonder how many people understand a sanctuary city is. Here's the deal.

  • It accepts the fact that there are people living in the city who are not there legally.
  • They want these people to be able to call the local police without fear of being turned into the feds. Otherwise the idea of crime going unreported would create much larger problems.
  • They want the children of these people, who are American citizens, to be able to go to school, again without having the parents reported to the feds for deportation. If they didn't guarantee that, the kids wouldn't be in school, and we all lose by having uneducated adults, it's a core principle of this country that educated citizens are a good thing, and it's important.
  • They want them to be able to get health care, to go to a hospital when someone is seriously ill or injured. This is part of basic humanity.

The Republican talking points make it sound like local governments are weak or immoral or anti-American, which is not what's going on. You couldn't run a city with huge crimes commited against illegals because they would be so vulnerable, and kids need education, and everyone needs health care. Yet I hear the word used all the time in public discourse, and am concerned that most people don't know what it means.
